svg.title: Five flex sensors on a numbered breadboard, one divider per finger on A0 to A4
svg.desc: Uno 5V feeds a positive rail and Uno GND a negative rail. Five independent 10 kilohm flex/resistor dividers share those rails. Suggested finger mapping: index A0 on row 5, middle A1 on row 11, ring A2 on row 17, little A3 on row 23, thumb A4 on row 29. Rows a through e are connected internally; the f through j strips remain separate. Named Uno breakouts are not physical header positions.
svg.text: Five fingers · five independent dividers · Uno A0–A4
Suggested finger mapping · original breadboard reference · verify actual pin labels and rail continuity before power-up
Shared supply and ground; a separate signal junction for every finger
Dots mark wire endpoints. Insulated wires can cross strips/rails without joining them; only marked endpoints are inserted.
• Each flex strip is a passive 10 kΩ nominal reference part. Each fixed resistor is a separate 10 kΩ / 1% part.
• a–e holes on one row share a strip. f–j are isolated across the gap. Shown section: rows 1–33 of a suitable board.
• Connect every divider, then set kActiveFingers = 5, rebuild and recalibrate all fingers for the five-second session.
• Radios still use Uno 3.3V separately. This change adds sensing channels; the supplied receiver drives only finger 0.
Original SVG · MIT · Reference assembly, not a physical test. See the hardware guide for the full hole table and rail-continuity checks.
